# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: OSC title (0/1/2), clipboard write (52), cwd (7), prompt marks (133), handshake (1337)
# (issue #9, wave 7)   target path: crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/osc_spec.txt
# spec-researcher output (2026-10-30), finalised by the milestone lead 2026-10-30 (see LEAD DECISIONS below).
# ONLY THE MILESTONE LEAD EDITS THIS FILE. The implementer copies it verbatim and never edits a row: a row that
# looks wrong is REPORTED (row id, expected, actual, why) to the lead, who corrects it here.
#
# Same `###` row layout as modes_spec.txt / csi_spec.txt (### ID / size / step / cite / note / screen / cursor /
# pending_wrap / requests / scrollback). tests/osc.rs needs its OWN row parser (do NOT use tests/spec/mod.rs, which
# #143 is rewriting and whose parse_requests only knows Bell/Resize); keys the shared parser would reject are below.
#
# EXTRA / CHANGED KEYS (osc.rs must assert these by hand)
#   requests:  [] or a comma list of  Bell | SetTitle("..") | SetClipboard("..") | SetCwd(b"..") |
#              ShellIntegrationHandshake(b"..")      Strings use \xNN \\ \" \u{H..} \n \r \t escapes; b".." is Vec<u8>
#              (bytes), the others String. `Request` is #[non_exhaustive]: compare the WHOLE list in order.
#   marks:     semantic marks on the ACTIVE screen's rows, 0-based: `r0=[PromptStart,CommandStart] r2=[OutputStart]`;
#              rows not listed must have NO marks. Mark names: PromptStart CommandStart OutputStart CommandEnd(None)
#              CommandEnd(0) CommandEnd(130). Order inside [] = Line::marks order.
#   main_marks:     same, for the stashed main screen while the alt screen is active (hand-asserted via a leave).
#   marks_scrollback: `s0=[PromptStart]` s0 = oldest scrollback line.
#   screen:    `not asserted` is allowed; otherwise the render_screen layout (`|` after the cursor cell, `\` = soft wrap).
#   screen_is: main | alt          step kinds: feed <payload> | feed_bytewise <payload>   (one advance() call per byte)
#   layer:     term (default, row of osc.rs) | parse (a pure-function row for the app-core / grid / shell-integration
#              unit tests; NOT run by osc.rs)
# PAYLOAD ESCAPES in `step:`   \xNN raw byte  \r \n \t \\   \u{H..} one scalar UTF-8 encoded
#   HARNESS EXTENSIONS (osc.rs must add these to its decoder; they exist only so 1 MiB rows stay readable):
#     @rep(C,N)      N copies of the single ASCII char C                      @rep(a,1024)
#     @b64rep(C,N)   standard base64 (with padding) of N copies of byte C     @b64rep(a,1048576)
#   The same @rep(..) form is allowed inside requests: strings.
# EVERY ROW ALSO RUNS CHUNKED (lead 2026-10-30): whole / byte-at-a-time / every 2-way split for rows whose decoded
#   input is <= 512 bytes; rows above 512 bytes run whole + byte-at-a-time + 2-way splits at the first 16 and last 16
#   offsets; rows above 64 KiB (K32, K33) run whole + those 32 2-way splits only (no byte-at-a-time). Results must be
#   equal across chunkings. Rows flagged `chunk-skip` are exempt (none are).
#
# SOURCE TAGS (fetched 2026-10-30; line numbers are for the files as fetched)
#   [CTL]   xterm ctlseqs  https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html  (Operating System Commands; Ps=0/1/2/52)
#           (text read from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots/master/ctlseqs.txt L2008-L2200)
#   [XT-m]  xterm misc.c   do_osc L3988 (empty 0/1/2 data -> "xterm" L4126-4142; mode>65535 ignored), xtermIsPrintable L3427,
#           ChangeGroup L6125 (`strlen(value) > 1000` -> request IGNORED, not truncated),
#           ManipulateSelectionData L3320 (Pc parse: empty -> "s0", unknown letters skipped, `?` = query, else SET)
#   [XT-c]  xterm charproc.c  string collection L3395-3460 (strings_max, DEF_STRINGS_MAX 20000 | 600000 in ptyx.h/main.h,
#           over-long string IGNORED whole), CASE_BELL L3690, CASE_ST L5290 (OSC dispatched on BEL or ST only)
#   [XT-b]  xterm button.c AppendToSelectionBuffer L4695 (base64 decoder SKIPS every non-alphabet byte, no padding needed)
#   [AL]    Alacritty: vte crate src/ansi.rs osc_dispatch L1331-1500 (0/2 join params with ';' and trim; 1, 7, 133, 1337 not
#           handled; 52 needs >=3 params, Pc = first byte of params[1] default 'c'); alacritty_terminal term/mod.rs
#           clipboard_store (c -> Clipboard, p|s -> Selection, else return; base64 decode failure or non-UTF-8 -> nothing;
#           default Osc52 = OnlyCopy; no size cap)
#   [WZ]    WezTerm wezterm-escape-parser/src/osc.rs L100-185 (Selection::try_parse: empty -> SELECT|CUT0, c p s 0-9;
#           2 params = ClearSelection, `?` = query, else STANDARD base64 + from_utf8, any failure = whole OSC dropped;
#           titles: params joined with ';'), term/src/terminalstate/performer.rs L741-800 (OSC 1 stores a separate
#           icon_title, OSC 0 sets both, OSC 2 title only; empty title stored as empty), L867-905 (133: fresh_line on A/D)
#   [KT]    kitty kitty/vt-parser.c dispatch_osc L520-660 (0 = title+icon, 1 = icon only, 2 = title; OSC 7 stores raw
#           bytes; 1337 = DESKTOP NOTIFY, not shell integration; 133 -> shell_prompt_marking), kitty/screen.c
#           shell_prompt_marking L3637 (A/C set ONE `prompt_kind` attribute on the CURSOR ROW `cursor->y`, pending wrap NOT
#           resolved, linebuf = current screen incl. alt; `A;k=s` -> SECONDARY_PROMPT which prompt navigation skips),
#           kitty/clipboard.py parse_osc_52 L490 + from_osc52_where_field L85 (c and s -> clipboard, p -> primary,
#           other letters dropped, empty Pc -> 's0'), kitty/options/definition.py clipboard_control (default:
#           write-clipboard write-primary read-clipboard-ask read-primary-ask), clipboard_max_size default 512 (MB)
#   [IT]    iTerm2 sources/VT100/VT100Terminal.m decodedBase64PasteCommand L1566 (Pc chars from "psc01234567" are all
#           accepted and IGNORED -> general pasteboard; unknown char = parse failure; `?` never answered by default;
#           decoded text has C0 controls other than TAB/LF/CR stripped and stops at NUL), XTERMCC_WIN_TITLE L2776
#           (title cut at newline, control chars -> ^X), executeXtermSetKvp L4418 (`ShellIntegrationVersion` key)
#   [BO]    Per Bothner / FinalTerm semantic prompts  https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/-/raw/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md
#           (A, B, C, D[;exit] plus L, N, P, I; options after ';'; `k=` kinds i c s r; unknown options ignored)
#   [VTE]   vte 0.15.0 src/lib.rs advance_osc_string L407, osc_dispatch L575, MAX_OSC_PARAMS = 16 L45, tests L930-1050
#   [VT]    crates/tessera-vt/src/lib.rs (osc_dispatch L278 drops `bell_terminated`; Action::Osc(Vec<Vec<u8>>) is the
#           payload SPLIT ON ';'; OSC length unbounded, docs L25-33)
#   [PROBE] ran a throw-away tessera-vt Parser on the exact bytes (scratchpad spec-researcher-9/probe), 2026-10-30
#   [CODE]  read/ran crates/tessera-shell-integration (parse_osc7, parse_osc1337, parse_osc133) at 2f07dff
#
# FACTS THE IMPLEMENTER MUST KNOW (all [PROBE]-verified)
#   1. Action::Osc carries the payload SPLIT ON ';' (`2;a;b` -> ["2","a","b"]). Title, OSC 7 and OSC 1337 payloads
#      contain ';' legitimately and must be REJOINED with ';' (params[1..].join(";")). Alacritty and WezTerm do the same.
#   2. vte keeps at most 16 params and silently drops everything after the 15th ';'. A payload with >= 15 ';' is truncated
#      with no flag. Rule D-PARAMS: params.len() == 16 means "possibly truncated".
#   3. vte silently drops C0 bytes 0x00-0x06, 0x08-0x17, 0x19, 0x1C-0x1F inside an OSC (TAB, LF, CR, NUL included), so a
#      title or base64 payload can never contain them. It does NOT drop DEL (0x7F) or UTF-8 C1 (U+0080..U+009F), and bytes
#      >= 0x80 are passed through whatever their validity.
#   4. CAN (0x18), SUB (0x1A) and ESC inside an OSC DISPATCH the OSC collected so far (vte osc_end) and then act on the
#      byte; xterm ABORTS the string without dispatching. The terminator is not visible in Action::Osc (dropped by [VT]).
#   5. Raw 0x9C and UTF-8 U+009C do NOT terminate an OSC in vte (they are appended), and 0x9D / U+009D does not start one.
#   6. ST arrives as Action::Osc followed by Action::Esc{byte:'\\'}; BEL as Action::Osc only. Neither may print or ring.
#
# DECISIONS FOR THE MILESTONE LEAD (recommendation first; every row that depends on one names it in `flags:`)
#   D-OSC1      OSC 1 (icon name). RECOMMEND: ignore, no Request (xterm sets only the icon name; WezTerm/kitty keep it
#               apart from the title; Alacritty ignores; iTerm2 shows it as the tab title only if so configured).
#               OSC 0 -> SetTitle, OSC 2 -> SetTitle. Rows T05, T05b.
#   D-EMPTY     `OSC 2 ; ST` (empty title). RECOMMEND: SetTitle("") (the Swift side already maps empty to the default
#               title, TerminalWindowController.sessionDidSetTitle). xterm shows its default "xterm" ([XT-m] L4126).
#               `OSC 2 ST` WITHOUT the ';' -> ignored (WezTerm, Alacritty; xterm also sets the default). Rows T07-T09.
#   D-TITLE-CAP Title cap. RECOMMEND 1024 bytes of payload (measured before sanitising); a longer title is IGNORED whole,
#               not truncated (xterm ChangeGroup: > 1000 bytes -> ignored; WezTerm/Alacritty/kitty: no cap). Alternative:
#               truncate at a char boundary. Rows T18-T20.
#   D-TITLE-SAN Title sanitising. RECOMMEND strip, after UTF-8 decoding: Cc (DEL, C1) and bidi/line-separator format
#               characters U+061C U+200E U+200F U+202A-U+202E U+2066-U+2069 U+2028 U+2029 (title spoofing in the tab
#               strip). vte already removed C0. Do not trim spaces (xterm keeps them; Alacritty trims). iTerm2 instead
#               cuts at the first newline and shows ^X for controls. Rows T14-T16, T21.
#   D-BADUTF8   Invalid UTF-8 in a title. RECOMMEND from_utf8_lossy (U+FFFD visible). WezTerm drops the whole OSC,
#               Alacritty drops the bad segment. Clipboard is the opposite: invalid UTF-8 is DROPPED (K27). Rows T17, X03.
#   D-OSCNUM    Command number matching. RECOMMEND exact ASCII match on the whole first param ("2", not "02", "+2").
#               xterm and kitty accept leading zeros. Row T31, U01.
#   D-CAN       CAN/SUB/ESC inside an OSC. RECOMMEND accept the vte behaviour (apply what was collected), because the
#               terminator is not visible in tessera-vt and the brief puts tessera-vt out of scope. xterm discards. Truncated
#               OSC 52 payloads are still caught by strict base64 (K38). If the lead wants the xterm behaviour, tessera-vt
#               must report the terminator (a follow-up to "vt: bound OSC payloads"). Rows T25-T27, X05, K37, K38.
#   D-PARAMS    params.len() == 16 (vte's cap) => possibly truncated. RECOMMEND: titles are applied as received
#               (best effort, T12); OSC 7 and OSC 1337 are DROPPED (a truncated path is a different valid path). Rows W05, H08.
#   D-FWD-CAP   Raw-forwarded requests (SetCwd, ShellIntegrationHandshake): RECOMMEND the terminal drops payloads longer
#               than 4096 bytes (= tessera_shell_integration::osc7::MAX_OSC7_LEN) and empty payloads, so a flood cannot
#               queue megabytes; app-core still parses with parse_osc7 / parse_osc1337. Rows W06-W08, H07.
#   D-1337      OSC 1337 forwards ONLY payloads starting with `ShellIntegrationVersion=`; every other OSC 1337 key (File=
#               with megabytes of image data, SetUserVar, CurrentDir, RequestAttention, ReportCellSize query, ...) is
#               ignored and NEVER answered. The brief says "OSC 1337 handshake" so this is consistent, but the term
#               layer must do the prefix test, not app-core. Rows H05, H06.
#   D-SEL       OSC 52 selection parameter Pc. RECOMMEND: Pc empty, or containing at least one of c p s -> write the macOS
#               general pasteboard once (duplicates collapse, c0/0c/sp fine); Pc made only of q and 0-7 -> ignore; ANY
#               character outside {c p q s 0-7} -> ignore the whole sequence (iTerm2 treats it as a parse failure; xterm and
#               kitty skip the letter). macOS has no primary selection, iTerm2 maps all of psc0-7 to the pasteboard,
#               kitty maps c and s to the clipboard and p to PRIMARY (absent on macOS), Alacritty maps c to the clipboard
#               and p/s to PRIMARY. Rows K01-K14.
#   D-EMPTY52   Empty data `52;c;` (and `52;c`). RECOMMEND: ignore, no request. xterm CLEARS the selection ([CTL] "neither a
#               base64 string nor ? then the selection is cleared"); WezTerm clears on `52;c`; kitty writes an empty
#               string; Alacritty ignores `52;c`. A remote program can overwrite the clipboard anyway, but wiping it
#               silently adds nothing the user asked for. Rows K18-K21.
#   D-B64       Base64. RECOMMEND strict RFC 4648 STANDARD alphabet, padding REQUIRED and canonical, no whitespace, no
#               URL-safe alphabet, trailing bits must be zero. Alacritty, WezTerm (allows non-zero trailing bits) and
#               kitty ("must not silently discard invalid characters") are strict; xterm skips junk. Rows K22-K26, K39, K40.
#   D-CAP52     OSC 52 size cap. RECOMMEND 1 MiB DECODED (1_048_576 bytes accepted, 1_048_577 dropped); reject before
#               decoding when the base64 length exceeds 1_398_104 (= 4*ceil(cap/3)). Survey: kitty 512 MB default
#               (clipboard_max_size), xterm string buffer 20000 bytes (600000 with sixel/regis builds, whole OSC
#               ignored), Alacritty / WezTerm / iTerm2: no cap found. NOTE tessera-vt still buffers an unbounded OSC (its
#               crate docs call it a known gap), so the cap bounds the Request, not the parser memory. Rows K32, K33.
#   D-CTRL52    Clipboard content. RECOMMEND pass through UNCHANGED (embedded NUL and ESC survive; the brief's FFI test
#               needs the NUL). iTerm2 strips C0 and stops at NUL; kitty/Alacritty/WezTerm do not. Rows K28, K29.
#   D-READ      `OSC 52 ; Pc ; ?` and every other query (CSI 21 t, OSC 1337 ReportCellSize, ...) is never answered.
#               Matches the brief; xterm answers only with allowWindowOps. Rows K15-K17, T35, H05.
#   D-PARAMS52  `52` must have exactly 3 params (name, Pc, data). 4+ params (data containing ';') and 2 params (`52;data`)
#               are ignored. Alacritty ignores the extra params, WezTerm rejects. Rows K34, K35.
#   D-SECOND    OSC 133 `A` with `k=s`, `k=c` or `k=r` (secondary/continuation/right prompt). RECOMMEND: no mark, so a PS2
#               never becomes a "previous prompt" target (kitty stores SECONDARY_PROMPT, which navigation skips). This
#               changes the doc of tessera_shell_integration::parse_osc133 ("A;k=s ... are ignored"), whose tests do not
#               cover it. If the lead prefers to keep PromptStart, flip rows M06b-M06d. Our zsh/fish scripts never emit k=.
#   D-STRICT133 OSC 133 letter must be followed by end or ';'. RECOMMEND strict (today's parse_osc133 matches any prefix:
#               `Afoo`, `AB` -> PromptStart, `D0` -> None). Letters L N P I Z and lower case -> None (not emitted by our
#               scripts; N/P are prompt variants of A and could be added later). Rows M07*, P133-*.
#   D-PENDING   A mark goes on the line the cursor is on when the OSC is PARSED, pending wrap is NOT resolved first
#               (kitty `cursor->y`; matches the brief "applies the mark to the cursor's line"). Rows M08, M09.
#   D-ALT       Marks received while the alternate screen is active are IGNORED (no scrollback exists there, the lines
#               vanish on leave, and a full-screen app's stray C/D must not confuse the main screen). kitty and WezTerm
#               record them on the alt screen but cannot navigate them. Equivalent after leaving. Rows M10, M11.
#   D-DUP       One mark of each kind per line: a new mark REPLACES an existing mark of the same variant on that line
#               (so a redrawn prompt, `D;1` then `D;0`, does not pile up) and is pushed last. kitty keeps one value per
#               line. Rows M13, M14.
#   D-FRESH     133;A does NOT fresh-line / move the cursor (Bothner's spec and WezTerm do; kitty and iTerm2 do not; our
#               scripts end the previous line themselves). Row M16.
#   D-HOST      OSC 7 host check (app-core, not term). RECOMMEND: App::session_cwd returns every valid report with its host;
#               add Cwd::is_local(local_hostname) (empty host, "localhost", or the machine's hostname compared ASCII-case-
#               insensitively, also ignoring a trailing ".local"/".lan"-style domain difference) and let consumers
#               (new tab in same directory) require it. Not verified how Terminal.app/WezTerm/kitty compare hosts.
#   D-HANDSHAKE major version mismatch = `version != scripts::PROTOCOL_VERSION` (1): the version is a single integer, so
#               "major" is the integer. tracing::warn! once per session. iTerm2's own scripts send 18..: parse OK, warn.
#   D-FLOOD     Do NOT coalesce requests in the terminal (T22 keeps order); the reader already hands them to app-core, whose
#               delivery path is coalescing (CallbackBridge). Requests per advance() are bounded by the input length.
#   D-TSTACK    CSI 22/23 t title stack and CSI 20/21 t title report are OUT of scope: they must stay unanswered no-ops
#               (T35, T36). Reporting titles back is the classic escape-injection vector; do not add it.
#
# UNVERIFIED FACTS (rows depending on them; everything else was read from source or [PROBE]/[CODE]-run)
#   * T16 (bidi/line-separator stripping): Tessera hardening, no reference emulator does it.
#   * X04, T02, X08, M10, M11: checked by the lead 2026-10-30 at 9c41758 by reading (not run): control.rs execute
#     ignores 0x9D (catch-all arm), esc.rs ignores ESC \ (catch-all arm), Grid::enter_alt_screen keeps the cursor
#     and leave_alt_screen (1049 reset) restores it.
#   * T25-T27, T33, X05, K37, K38: xterm's ESC/CAN behaviour inside an OSC inferred from charproc.c state handling;
#     the generated sos_table (VTPrsTbl.c) was not read. The vte side is [PROBE]-verified.
#   * D-HOST / L05: how Terminal.app, kitty and WezTerm compare the OSC 7 host was not read.
#   * All screen:/cursor: lines were computed by hand from the render_screen layout and never run against osc.rs.
# =============================================================================
#
# LEAD DECISIONS (2026-10-30)
#   Accepted as recommended: D-OSC1 D-EMPTY D-TITLE-CAP D-BADUTF8 D-OSCNUM D-CAN D-PARAMS D-FWD-CAP D-1337 D-SEL
#     D-EMPTY52 D-B64 D-CAP52 D-CTRL52 D-READ D-PARAMS52 D-SECOND D-STRICT133 D-PENDING D-ALT D-DUP D-FRESH
#     D-HANDSHAKE D-FLOOD D-TSTACK, and P7-23 (leave parse_osc7 as it is).
#   PENDING (security policy, decided by the lead before #9 starts): D-TITLE-SAN (rows T14 T15 T16 T21) and D-HOST
#     (layer rows L04 L05, App::session_cwd / Cwd::is_local). Until then these rows are not final.
#   Harness rules for tests/osc.rs:
#     * `marks:` absent or `none` = no marks on any ACTIVE-screen row; `marks_scrollback:` absent = no marks on any
#       scrollback line. `cursor:` / `pending_wrap:` / `screen_is:` absent = not asserted.
#     * M10's `main_marks:` is asserted by feeding `\x1b[?1049l` after M10's other checks (M11 is the same check).
#     * Step payloads are NOT trimmed (M01 ends in a significant space). @rep/@b64rep expand in steps and in
#       requests: strings (K32 compares a 1 MiB string).
#     * K32 and K33 have the SAME base64 length (1_398_104): the pre-decode length check alone cannot drop K33;
#       the decoded-length check is what K33 tests.
#     * The test asserts 194 rows parsed: 138 `layer: term` rows run, 56 `layer: parse` rows counted and listed as
#       not run by osc.rs. Parse rows are hand-transcribed into unit tests (P133-* next to Mark::from_osc133 in
#       tessera-grid; P7-* and P1337-* in tessera-shell-integration where not already covered), each test naming its
#       row id; the critic checks coverage by id. L01-L07 are app-core / FFI / Swift tests listed in the brief.
#   print_c0_spec.txt F04 and G08 (below): the #9 PR changes exactly those two rows' `requests:` lines (F04 ->
#     [SetTitle("title")], G08 -> [SetTitle("hi")]) and G08's `assert:` line, their two print snapshots and
#     print.rs's Bell-only request parser; this is a lead-sanctioned edit (#143 has merged). No other row changes.
#
# WHERE THE BRIEF / EXISTING FILES CONFLICT WITH THE SOURCES
#   * print_c0_spec.txt rows F04 and G08 (and tests/scripts/print/f04_*, g08_*) expect `requests: []` for
#     `ESC ] 2;title BEL` / `ESC ] 0;hi ST`; both will start producing SetTitle. Their notes already say "superseded by #9",
#     but the #143/#113 do_not_touch lists keep fixtures byte-identical: #9 must edit those two rows (and print.rs's
#     bell-only requests check) in the same PR, or #143 must be told.
#   * The brief says OSC 1337 requests carry "the handshake"; kitty uses OSC 1337 for notifications and iTerm2 for many
#     other keys, so D-1337 (prefix filter in the term layer) is needed to avoid forwarding image data.
#   * The brief's "bound OSC" is not done in tessera-vt (D-CAP52 note): memory stays unbounded in the parser.
#   * `parse_osc133` today matches by prefix (`Afoo` is a mark) - see D-STRICT133 and D-SECOND.
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- T. OSC 0 / 1 / 2 window and icon title

### T01_osc2_bel
size: 2x40
step: feed \x1b]2;hello\x07
cite: [CTL] Ps=2 'Change Window Title to Pt'; [XT-m] do_osc OSC_TitleOnly -> ChangeTitle; BEL terminator [CTL] 'XTerm accepts either BEL or ST'
screen:

>

pending_wrap: false
requests: [SetTitle("hello")]

note: The ESC \ that ends the string must not print and must not move the cursor.

### T09_osc2_without_semicolon
size: 2x40

>
